metadata.title: Origami - How To Make An Origami Fox
metadata.description:
In this tutorial, I explain how to make an origami fox. I 
used square sheet of paper 15x15 cm or 6x6 inches.

During this tutorial just follow the instructions for folding the paper showed on upper left corner.If you have problems with keeping up  I recommend to pause the video until you make the following step, but in your own pace. 
If you need some help for folding your origami fox just ask 
I will help if I can!

Hope you enjoy, and please comment, share, and subscribe to my videos! 

Thanks :-)

transcript.text: Step 1: Fold paper in half diagonally and unfold
Step 2: Fold paper in half diagonally on other side
Step 3: Fold left and right side to meet the center line
Step 5: Fold all the layers diagonally
Step 6: Open up one layer to the right
Step 7: Open up the middle layer and squash fold to flatten the head
Step 8: Roll up the tail so the fox can stand up

summary.brief: Hands fold an orange sheet of paper into a standing origami fox and then show thank‑you and subscription graphics.
summary.detailed: The video begins with a title card that displays the text “Origami How To” and the dimensions of an orange square sheet (15 cm × 15 cm). A pair of hands appears over a white tabletop and starts folding the paper, first making diagonal creases to create triangles, then flipping and refolding as guided by small instructional diagrams in the upper‑left corner. summary.brief: Hands fold an orange square into a standing origami fox while on‑screen diagrams guide each step.

An orange square sheet is placed on a white surface and a pair of hands appear, holding the paper with the index, middle fingers and thumbs. They fold the left and right edges to the center line, then fold the paper in half, and fold all layers along a diagonal again. A layer is opened to the right and a squash‑fold is performed to shape the fox’s head. The tail is rolled and shaped, and the model is gently pressed and adjusted until it stands upright as an orange origami fox. The sequence ends with a “NEXT WEEK” graphic and a preview of the next paper project.
